step1_figure.circuit_type: Switched-Capacitor Sample-and-Hold Circuit with Fully-Differential Two-Stage Op-Amp with CMFB
step1_figure.description: Figure 26.25 shows the switched-capacitor sample-and-hold circuit topology with non-overlapping clocks (phi1, phi2, phi3) and 250 fF sampling/load capacitors. The core amplifier used is the two-stage fully-differential op-amp with CMFB and cascoded NMOS output buffers shown in Figure 26.33 (simulated in Figure 26.36).

output_cm_voltage.description: DC output common-mode voltage maintained by the CMFB loop under steady-state operation

equation.explanation: The continuous-time common-mode feedback (CMFB) circuit senses the output common-mode level via resistive averaging (20k resistors) and compares it to VCM (500 mV), holding the outputs centered at VCM without wandering.
equation.assumptions: CMFB loop is settled and stable.

sky130_expected.calculation: VCM is set to 500 mV in the schematic netlist. With high CMFB loop gain (around 200), the loop forces VOCM to equal VCM = 0.500 V with < 15 mV offset.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Finite CMFB loop gain and systematic input offsets result in a settled common-mode voltage very close to 0.5 V.

differential_open_loop_gain.description: Small-signal differential open-loop voltage gain (A_OL = d(vop - vom)/d(vp - vm)) of the op-amp core

equation.formula: A_{OL} = g_{m1,2} \cdot (r_{on} \parallel r_{op}) \cdot g_{m,out} \cdot (r_{on,out} \parallel r_{op,out} \parallel R_{CMFB})
equation.explanation: Differential gain of the two-stage amplifier loaded by the 20k CMFB resistive divider network and cascode output stages.
equation.assumptions: Output stage operating in saturation; small-signal differential excitation around 500 mV common-mode.

sky130_expected.calculation: In Figure 26.34, the simulated DC deriv(vop-vom) peaks at ~360 V/V (51.1 dB). In SKY130 with 20k resistive loading, the output resistance is bounded by ~10k (two 20k resistors in parallel to AC ground), giving gm,out * Rout ~ 5-10 and first stage gain ~ 30-50, resulting in overall gain ~ 200-400 V/V (46 - 52 dB).
sky130_expected.reasoning: Text explicitly states the gain is in the hundreds (Figure 26.34 shows a peak value of ~360).

cmfb_forward_gain.description: Gain from the CMFB control input VCMFB to the op-amp outputs

equation.explanation: Gain seen by the CMFB voltage injecting current into the center diff-pair node, shifting the first stage outputs and modulating the second stage gate bias.
equation.assumptions: All biasing devices operating in active/saturation region.

sky130_expected.calculation: A_CMFB-opamp is approximately 25 V/V (28 dB) as noted on page 882.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Text states the CMFB forward gain is approximately 25 (about 10 times less than the differential gain).

cmfb_amplifier_gain.description: Voltage gain of the error diff-amp with current-mirror load used for CMFB

equation.explanation: Small-signal gain from the averaged output node VCMA to the node VCMFB.

sky130_expected.calculation: Text states on page 882: 'Using the diff-amp with current mirror load, Fig. 26.28b, gives a gain of approximately 8' (18 dB).
sky130_expected.reasoning: Explicitly stated as 8 V/V in textbook.

cmfb_loop_gain.description: Total open-loop gain of the CMFB feedback control loop

equation.explanation: Product of the error amplifier gain and the op-amp CMFB-to-output gain.
equation.assumptions: Unbroken feedback loop with resistive common-mode detector.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Stated on page 882: 'combined with the op-amp's CMFB gain gives an overall CMFB loop gain of 200'.

total_quiescent_current.description: Total DC supply current drawn from VDD

equation.explanation: Calculated by summing the current of all branches (11 branches in op-amp and CMFB stage, counting doubled output widths, plus 50 uA for the reference bias circuit).
equation.assumptions: Nominal branch currents of 20 uA, bias circuit sinking ~50 uA.

sky130_expected.calculation: I_DD = 11 * 20 uA + 50 uA = 270 uA nominal (can vary between 250 uA and 450 uA depending on VDD and MOSFET saturation points).
sky130_expected.reasoning: Text notes nominal estimate of 270 uA; with the modified buffer (Fig. 26.33), excess current over-drain seen in Fig. 26.29 is reduced.

equation.explanation: With the cascoded NMOS in the modified buffer of Figure 26.32/26.33, the outputs swing close to the power supply rails (unlike the limited 200 mV - 800 mV swing of Figure 26.30).
equation.assumptions: Output devices remain in active or boundary-triode region.

sky130_expected.calculation: For VDD=1.8V, V_swing covers from ~0.15 V to ~1.65 V single-ended, giving a swing > 1.4 V.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Cascode buffer restores rail-to-rail swing as demonstrated in Fig. 26.34.

step3_testbench.description: Simulation testbench for switched-capacitor S/H circuit and op-amp characterization measuring DC operating point, total power, output common-mode level, and transient sample-and-hold behavior.
